papers.title: Sleep pressure is increased by protein fragments and decreased by processive proteolysis.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: Using zebrafish, the authors tested predictions of the fragment generation hypothesis and found that caspase inhibition decreased sleep while proteasome inhibition increased sleep, with calpain inhibition reducing proteasome-inhibitor-induced sleep and rebound sleep after deprivation. These results support protein fragments generated by proteases as a molecular source of homeostatic sleep pressure.

papers.title: NED-Net: open-source software for building and refining seizure detectors during rodent EEG experiments
papers.summary: The authors introduce NED-Net, open-source software for training and maintaining rodent EEG seizure detectors through an annotation-training loop that retrains on reviewed candidate events as annotations accumulate. A detector trained on one mouse cohort reached 93.6% precision, but failed to generalize (median per-animal recall 10%), and retraining with second-cohort annotations raised convulsive recall from 15% to 64%, detecting at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.summary: LogicSleep is a neurosymbolic framework combining a CNN-graph U-Net backbone with Conditional Random Fields and differentiable-logic transition rules for explainable, physiologically plausible, subject-adaptive sleep staging. Across ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 in within- and cross-dataset settings it consistently outperformed strong baselines and improved sequence-level metrics.

papers.title: The insular cortex and arousal: insights from a human focal lesion-based model.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In 46 patients undergoing awake craniotomy for insular gliomas, transient intraoperative episodes of impaired task engagement (intra-surgical falling asleep phenomenon, ISFAP) occurred in 22 and were accompanied by NREM-like EEG/ECoG patterns including theta-delta slow waves and spindle-like activity. Right-sided tumors and train-of-five stimulation were associated with ISFAP in univariate but not multivariable analyses, suggesting transient arousal instability from lesion-related network dysfunction.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.summary: High-density EEG and spectral/complexity measures characterized eight jhana advanced concentration absorption states in 20 advanced meditators. ACAM-J showed posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all states, and increased entropy-based complexity, with complexity remaining elevated even in late minimal states.

papers.title: The chronobiology of brain waste clearance: Sleep-wake and circadian regulation of glymphatic function.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic evidence on the glymphatic system, framing glymphatic efficiency as a chronobiologically regulated dimension of sleep quality driven by sleep-wake state, circadian clocks, and locus coeruleus norepinephrine oscillations. It evaluates biomarkers such as DTI-ALPS and plasma waste markers and proposes incorporating glymphatic endpoints into sleep and chronobiology trials.

papers.title: Sleep-Deprivation Serum Induces Mitochondrial Stress in BV2 Cells: Responses to P2Y12-Targeted Pharmacological Modulation.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Using an in vitro serum-transfer model, serum from sleep-deprived mice reduced mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1 ratio), shortened mitochondrial networks, and suppressed Rhod-2 calcium responses in BV2 microglia. P2Y12 antagonist MRS2395 and agonist 2-MeSADP failed to consistently restore mitochondrial or calcium response profiles under sleep-deprivation serum, linking sleep-loss circulating factors to microglial mitochondrial stress and altered purinergic responsiveness.

papers.title: Psychedelics and Sleep: Preclinical and Human Studies-A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review of 12 preclinical and clinical studies found that classic psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT/ayahuasca) consistently produce acute REM sleep suppression, delayed REM onset, and increased wakefulness in preclinical work, with heterogeneous human findings including prolonged REM latency after psilocybin and reduced REM duration after ayahuasca. Evidence on slow-wave activity was mixed, and included studies showed fair-to-poor validity and notable risk of bias.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.summary: Reviews data-driven EEG-fMRI fusion methods published between 2000 and 2025, organizing them by fusion strategy (symmetric vs. asymmetric), methodological objective (factorization vs. translation), and modeling assumptions (linear vs. nonlinear). It reports that no universal validation standard exists and that interpreting latent multimodal components remains difficult, while fusion has revealed distributed network dynamics not accessible through unimodal analyses.

papers.title: Brainstem Circuits Engaged During REM Sleep Regulate Apnea Susceptibility.
papers.summary: The authors show that preBötzinger Complex neurons and preBötC-projecting lateral parabrachial nucleus neurons selectively increase calcium activity during REM sleep, and that inhibiting or activating these neurons preferentially disrupts breathing and increases apnea susceptibility during REM sleep. This identifies state-dependent brainstem circuits underlying REM-specific respiratory vulnerability.

papers.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
papers.summary: The authors developed PSG-GAN, a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments capturing obstructive sleep apnea dynamics, including photoplethysmography-based heart-rate changes during and after breathing obstructions. An automatic scoring model trained solely on synthetic signals reached good sleep staging (kappa 0.71 and 0.63) and respiratory event segmentation (kappa 0.57 and 0.60) on test sets of healthy volunteers and OSA patients.

papers.title: Circadian modulation of dopamine release shapes reward-evoked signaling in the nucleus accumbens.
papers.summary: Long-term fiber photometry with the DA3m sensor in C57BL/6J mice showed that spontaneous nucleus accumbens dopamine peaked in the early subjective day, reward-evoked dopamine peaked at the day-to-night transition, and cue-evoked dopamine and reward behavior peaked in the early subjective night. SCN-specific Bmal1 disruption attenuated spontaneous dopamine rhythmicity, and reward-evoked dopamine was positively associated with reward behavior and cue-evoked dopamine but negatively associated with pre-reward baseline dopamine.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional comparison plus a 12-week uncontrolled before-after exercise intervention in permanent night-shift workers, habitually active workers showed greater activity-rest rhythm amplitude, dominant periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization than sedentary workers, with similar pre-to-post changes in the intervention group. Weekend recovery transiently shortened dominant periods to ~18-22 h with acrophase shifts toward diurnal timing, interpreted as adaptive circadian reorganization; the lack of a control group limits causal attribution.

papers.title: Influence of social housing on dim light at night induced behavioural and hepatic alterations in mice.
papers.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
papers.summary: In male mice exposed to dim light at night (DLAN) or a standard light-dark cycle for 28 days, social isolation exacerbated DLAN-induced anxiety-like behaviour, anhedonia, oxidative stress, and hepatic injury, whereas group housing attenuated these behavioural and hepatic deficits and improved antioxidant status.

papers.title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine sedation in pediatric electroencephalography: dose optimization, safety, and EEG characteristics.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 224 children undergoing EEG, intranasal dexmedetomidine achieved 94.6–94.7% initial sedation success with 10-minute onset and mild, self-limited adverse events in ~3%. In an 11-patient paired subgroup, no significant spectral power differences versus chloral hydrate were detected, though equivalence could not be established.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial that will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3 sleep-onset chronic insomnia to compare a 12-week Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method intervention against CBT-I, with PSQI change at week 12 as the primary endpoint. Secondary and exploratory endpoints integrate clinical scales, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI/EEG measures of cortical network connectivity to test efficacy and mechanisms.

papers.title: From sleep complaints to clinical phenotypes: A tiered assessment and integrated management framework for sleep comorbidities in Epilepsy-A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a complaint-based clinical framework for identifying, tiered assessing, and integratively managing sleep comorbidities in epilepsy, organizing insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome/periodic limb movements, excessive daytime sleepiness, and overlap phenotypes across life-course and epilepsy-syndrome contexts. The framework links sleep complaints to phenotype recognition, objective testing, phenotype-specific intervention, and follow-up reassessment, but its feasibility and outcome effects remain to be prospectively evaluated.

papers.title: Behavioural sleep quality and quantity and their associations with age, salivary cortisol and abnormal behaviours: A preliminary field study in racing thoroughbreds.
papers.summary: This 48-hour field study quantified behavioral NREM-like and REM-like sleep and sleep interruptions in 13 training Thoroughbred racehorses and related sleep measures to age, salivary cortisol, and abnormal behaviors. Age was associated with sleep quantity, while lower sleep quality indices were linked to higher morning cortisol and more frequent abnormal behaviors.

papers.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG sleep staging using a serpentine dataflow that reduces memory accesses 6.2× and 2.25× over output- and weight-stationary dataflows, plus hybrid dynamic quantization reducing model size 4.16×. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, it consumes 0.40 mW and stays within 0.15% of floating-point accuracy on MASS-SS3 leave-two-subject-out validation.

papers.title: Non-coding RNAs in circadian network regulation and disease: from oscillatory coupling to precision chronomedicine.
papers.journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and circular RNAs are integral to the circadian transcription-translation feedback loop, modulating core clock genes, entrainment, and central-peripheral oscillator coupling. It argues that ncRNA-clock disruption destabilizes oscillatory amplitude and phase coherence, contributing to metabolic, neuropsychiatric, inflammatory, and neoplastic disease, and frames circadian dysfunction as network instability relevant to chronomedicine.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.summary: Using EEG from 1,534 participants aged 5–21 years during a contrast-change discrimination task, this study combined neural measures of visual response and evidence accumulation with decision modeling to show that perceptual decision accuracy matures earlier than speed. Accuracy improved via fewer attention lapses and more efficient accumulation (half of developmental change by about age 9), whereas non-decision time shortened only between ages 11 and 14, indicating dissociable maturation of decision components.

papers.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice.
papers.summary: In male mice exposed to intermittent hypoxia for 7–210 days, the authors found tissue-specific DNA methylation changes (5,747 DMPs in left ventricle, 1,307 in PBMCs) and epigenetic age acceleration, with Cdkn2a/p16 senescence implicated in vascular dysfunction. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve.

papers.title: Circadian disruption worsens postseptic pulmonary fibrotic remodeling through a CLOCK/PIEZO1-linked myeloid immunometabolic program.
papers.summary: Using patient lung specimens, murine transcriptomic datasets, and cecal ligation and puncture with shifted light-dark cycles, this study showed that circadian disruption suppresses macrophage CLOCK, derepresses PIEZO1, impairs lipophagy, and promotes PAD4-dependent extracellular trap formation, aggravating post-septic pulmonary fibrosis; myeloid Piezo1 deletion attenuated fibrosis.

papers.title: Association of Newer Glucose-Lowering Medications and Phenoconversion From REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder to Parkinsonian Disorders in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.summary: In a target trial emulation using Medicare claims among older adults with REM sleep behavior disorder and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1 receptor agonist and SGLT-2 inhibitor use were each associated with lower risk of incident Parkinson's disease and parkinsonism versus DPP-4 inhibitors, but not dementia with Lewy bodies; no significant difference was seen between GLP-1RAs and SGLT-2is.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Circadian Dysregulation in the Choroid Plexus of a Nitroglycerin Rat Model of Chronic Migraine: An RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.journal: Journal of central nervous system disease
papers.summary: This RNA-seq study profiled choroid plexus circadian gene expression in a nitroglycerin rat model of chronic migraine versus saline controls and reported sex-specific transcriptomic changes, including upregulated antioxidant genes (MT2A, SLC7A11) in females and inflammatory factors (ZBTB16, S100A8) in males. Circadian genes were dysregulated (e.g., SERPINE1 upregulated, PER2 downregulated), with enriched circadian rhythm, HIF-1 signaling (females), inflammatory, lipid metabolism, and heme pathways.

papers.title: Sleep quality moderating the relationship between hearing loss and cognition in older adults: Implications for Alzheimer's disease risk.
papers.summary: Examined whether sleep quality moderates the association between hearing impairment and cognition in 122 older adults from the MedWalk study. Poorer sleep quality strengthened associations between peripheral hearing loss and associative learning errors and between speech-in-noise performance and spatial working memory errors, suggesting domain-specific interactions relevant to Alzheimer's disease risk.

papers.title: Extreme delta brush as an ictal pattern in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This case report describes a 22-year-old man with anti-NMDAR encephalitis in whom continuous EEG showed extreme delta brush complexes time-locked to stereotyped motor events (right jaw movement and right arm internal rotation), indicating that EDB can be an ictal pattern rather than only a non-ictal biomarker. The case highlights overlap between seizures and dyskinesias and the value of continuous EEG for distinguishing electroclinical seizures from dyskinetic movements.

papers.title: Analysis of nighttime heart rate variability during rapid eye movement and non-rapid eye movement in OSA.
papers.summary: In a retrospective polysomnography study of 373 patients with OSA, REM-related OSA in males with mild-to-moderate disease was independently associated with lower LFnu and LF/HF and higher HFnu during N1 and N2 sleep, whereas autonomic differences were absent in women and in REM sleep, indicating sex- and severity-dependent autonomic profiles.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Occupational Stress, and Work-related Determinants of Sleep Disturbance Among Practicing Physicians: A Cross-sectional Study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional survey of 627 practicing physicians assessing sleep patterns, lifestyle, and work-related stressors, finding that 54.1% slept ≤6 hours per night and 51.9% had sleep disturbance at least twice weekly. Sleep deprivation and disturbance were associated with work-related stressors such as poor work-life balance and administrative burden rather than lifestyle factors.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a girl with a de novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant causing NEDHIB who showed neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia-like nodding episodes, with marked motor and cognitive improvement and complete resolution of nodding after low-dose levodopa-benserazide.

papers.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
papers.summary: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational microlongitudinal feasibility protocol for 25 mother-child dyads (children aged 11-14) combining Garmin wearables, passive smartphone sensing, ecological momentary assessment, and mobile cognitive testing over 4 weeks to assess feasibility and explore within-person and dyadic associations among health behaviors, cognition, and momentary anxiety.

papers.title: Suspected Functional Adrenal Insufficiency and Unmasking of Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: A Case for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Restraint.
papers.journal: Clinical medicine insights. Endocrinology and diabetes
papers.summary: This case report describes a man with suspected secondary adrenal insufficiency following migration and night shift work whose symptoms and biochemistry resolved after sleep restoration and nutritional rehabilitation without glucocorticoids, with Hashimoto's thyroiditis unmasked at six-month follow-up.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and short-chain fatty acids in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Comparing 29 iRBD, 24 PD with RBD, 17 PD without RBD, and 18 controls, this study found shared gut dysbiosis (enriched Bifidobacterium, Blautia_A, Azospira_A; reduced Agathobaculum, Clostridium_Q, and others) and decreased fecal butyric and propionic acid in iRBD and PD with RBD, with correlations to clinical severity scales.

papers.title: Circadian orchestration of the cutaneous microenvironment and chronotherapeutic strategies in inflammatory skin diseases.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the circadian mechanisms linking epidermal barrier function and the local immune microenvironment in inflammatory skin diseases (atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, chronic spontaneous urticaria), and proposes a chronotherapeutic framework aligning administration timing of topical agents, systemic drugs, small molecules, and biologics with circadian peaks of their targets. It distinguishes clinically supported timing effects from remaining hypotheses and offers a testable framework for future chronotherapy research.

papers.title: Deciphering mitochondrial dysfunction and circadian rhythm-related pathogenic patterns for the pathogenesis of Kawasaki Disease and corresponding nursing therapeutic enrichment: Evidence from machine learning-driven multi-omics and clinical validation.
papers.summary: Used machine learning-driven multi-omics analyses of Kawasaki Disease transcriptomic datasets to identify a mitochondrial transport and circadian rhythm-related molecular signature, stratifying patients into two molecular subgroups. FNDC5 was nominated as a hub pathogenic factor validated by q-RT-PCR in clinical samples, with BRD-K10482608 computationally predicted as a candidate therapeutic.

papers.title: Changes in negative affect and resting-state EEG power following an EEG-derived generative reality art experience: a pilot pre-post study.
papers.summary: Exploratory pilot pre-post study of 30 healthy university students examined an EEG-derived generative virtual reality art experience, finding decreased negative affect and reduced resting-state absolute alpha- and beta-band power after a single 5-minute session. Changes in EEG measures were not associated with affect changes, and the single-group design precludes causal or therapeutic conclusions.

papers.title: The regenerative hexagon: six domains shaping musculoskeletal regenerative outcomes.
papers.summary: Proposes a "Regenerative Hexagon" framework that extends the classical scaffold-cells-growth factors triad with three host-state domains (Systemic Host Environment, Biomechanics/Mechanotransduction, Cellular Energetics), and grades evidence for each component, hypothesizing multiplicative interactions among pillars. Frames the model as a hypothesis-generating instrument rather than a validated clinical tool.

papers.title: Atypical delusional misidentification with alternating impostors in a single body: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 42-year-old woman with persecutory and grandiose delusions who believed different individuals alternately inhabited her husband's unchanged body, expressing full conviction without insight despite unremarkable neurological and routine laboratory findings. The presentation shares features with Capgras and Fregoli syndromes but fits neither, suggesting disturbed continuity of perceived personal identity rather than facial recognition alone.

papers.title: Navigating the diagnostic challenges of maladaptive daydreaming: a case report of ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic obsessive fantasies with functional impairment in a 17-year-old.
papers.summary: Case report of a 17-year-old female with maladaptive daydreaming (MDS-16 score 76%) presenting intrusive ego-syntonic and ego-dystonic fantasies, sleep disturbance, and functional decline, with unremarkable medical and neuroimaging workup. Describes differential diagnostic challenges versus OCD, ASD, and schizophrenia prodrome and gradual improvement on quetiapine plus CBT, occupational therapy, and family psychoeducation.

papers.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Reversible Rapidly Progressive Dementia Associated With ASIA Syndrome Secondary to Silicone Implants.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 33-year-old woman with bilateral silicone breast implants who developed rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, and polyarthralgia, with breast MRI revealing intracapsular rupture of both implants. Symptoms resolved completely by the seventh postoperative day after implant removal with complete capsulectomy, consistent with reversible dementia secondary to ASIA syndrome.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
